title: Curves of constant width and Lebesgue's covering problem
summary: A universal cover is a convex set in the plane that contains a congruent copy of every planar set of diameter one. Lebesgue asked in 1914 for one of least area, and the value is not known. We prove that every convex universal cover has area at least 0.8344, improving on 0.832, published in 2005, and 0.833, in a 2026 preprint, both of which come from a disc together with an equilateral triangle and a regular pentagon.
